           WEEK 6: ASSIGNMENT 6


     1. What  is  the fundamental assumption behind  the  k-Nearest
       Neighbors (k-NN) algorithm?
      A) Data points far apart in feature space will have similar outputs
       B) Similar instances are located near each other in feature space
       and will have similar outputs
       C) All data points have equal probability of any class
      D) The algorithm needs no training data at all
       Answer: B
       Refer to Lecture 26: Fundamentals of Machine Learning-I Slide
       15


     2. What distinguishes classification from regression as two types of
        supervised learning?
      A) Classification predicts continuous numeric values; regression
        predicts class labels
       B) Classification predicts a class label; regression predicts a
        continuous numerical value
       C) Both predict continuous numeric values
      D) Both predict continuous class labels
       Answer: B
       Refer to Lecture 26: Fundamentals of Machine Learning-I Slide
       14


     3. What fundamentally distinguishes unsupervised learning from
        supervised learning?
      A) Unsupervised learning uses more computational power
       B) Unsupervised learning is used only for classification, while
        supervised learning is used only for clustering.
       C) Unsupervised learning learns from unlabeled  data, while
        supervised learning learns from labeled data.

4. What is the geometric shape the linear regression algorithm aims
   to create when there are two input features?
  A) A straight line
   B) A plane
   C) A hyperplane
  D) A cluster centroid
   Answer: B
   Refer to Lecture 27: Fundamentals of Machine Learning-II Slide
   6


5. In the supervised learning, what is the specific purpose of the
  command .fit(X, y)?
  A) To generate new synthetic data for training.
   B) To import the supervised learning algorithm from the library.
   C) Feed (X,y) labeled data into model for training
  D) To test the model's accuracy on a separate dataset.
   Answer: C

   The .fit() method in Scikit-Learn is the standard way to train a
   model. It takes the input data (features X) and the known correct
   answers (targets y) and feed indo model for training.


6. What is the main difference between NumPy arrays and pandas
   DataFrames regarding data types?
  A) NumPy arrays can only contain integers, while DataFrames
   can only contain strings.
   B) NumPy arrays require all elements to be the same type, while
   DataFrames allow each column to have a different type.
   C) DataFrames require all elements to be the same type, while
  NumPy arrays allow each column to have a different type.

    partitions the training data. At a particular leaf node (terminal

   based on their target values 𝑦= [12,15,18,20,25].

    this leaf node, its predicted target value 𝑦̂ will be _________.
   Answer: 18.0

slides.text:
The output for a new data point with features 𝑥1 = 12 and 𝑥2 =
  3 is _______________.
   Answer: 14
   At Root Node: 𝑥1 ≤10?, it will Right (as 12 ≤10 is False)
   At Decision Node: 𝑥2 ≤5?, it will go Left (as 3 ≤5 is True)
   Target Location: Leaf Node 2

   For Regression tree: prediction is the mean (average) of the
    training instances that fall within that specific region (leaf node)


                                  10+14+18   42
   Predicted Value 𝑦̂ = 𝑚𝑒𝑎𝑛(𝑦) =     =  = 14.0
                                        3       3



9. The "brain" of the agent, which defines its behavior by mapping
   environmental states to actions, is known as the:
   A) Reward Function
   B) Policy
   C) Value Function
   D) Mode
   Answer: B
   Refer to Lecture 30: Reinforcement Learning Slide 11
